subject: Dev-to-prod bridge: SLA, timeouts, and rate-limit playbook
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cleverbank.com>, Nora King <nora@cleverbank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Dev-to-prod bridge: SLA, timeouts, and rate-limit playbook

Hi Samir / Nora,

Thanks again for the product demo earlier — excited to get CleverBank moved from PoC to production. This thread captures the dev->prod bridge steps our Implementation team will run and the SDK/runtime guidance we recommend so the cutover is low-risk. Vanessa and Grace are on the thread for implementation coordination.

High-level goals:
- Keep user-facing latency below 300ms median for single-turn calls; degrade gracefully for long streaming responses.
- Avoid token-cost surprises during rollout (canary + sampling).
- Ensure robust client-side retries and rate-limit behavior to protect both sides.

Immediate plan (week 1):
1) Sandbox verification (you): integrate SDK v0.9.5 (or newer) and validate auth + streaming in staging.
2) Canaries: route 2% of live traffic to Redwood sandbox keys for 48h, monitor latency/cost.
3) Endpoint migration: we provide a compatibility path: /v1/generate -> /v1/generate?variant=prod-compact; you can switch host header or use our routing policy.
4) Full cutover with traffic shift and rollback windows.

Recommended SDK setup (quick):
- Use our official SDKs (Node / Python). Set connection timeout = 2s, read/request timeout = 20s for normal requests; for streaming set read timeout = 90s with keepalive.
- Enable automatic idempotency keys on mutating calls; SDK defaults to request-id header.
- Configure built-in rate-limit handler: max_inflight = 8 per host, local queue depth = 100.

Retries and timeouts (recommended default):
- Retry on 429 and 5xx only.
- Backoff: exponential with full jitter; base = 200ms, factor = 2.0, max backoff = 10s, max attempts = 4.
- For streaming endpoints do not retry mid-stream. Instead, fail-fast and surface a client-side resume token to the app.

Rate-limit handling (server semantics):
- 429 responses include headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch seconds).
- Use Remaining + Reset to shape the client leaky-bucket. If Remaining < 5, pause nonessential retries and surface a soft-failure to the UX.
- For heavy batch workloads prefer batch endpoints with token accounting to reduce header pressure.

Endpoint migration notes:
- We support pinned model variants. During migration, use the ?variant query param to test new kernels. Traffic policy example: route by header X-RW-Canary:true for 2% traffic.
- Recommended test: send 1000 synthetic requests that mirror your median sequence length, measure 95th percentile latency and token delta vs current.

Attachments: integration_config.yaml (yaml), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps: Vanessa will schedule the implementation kickoff. Can we target Monday 29 Nov for the first canary? If that works we'll send the DocuSign MSA and calendar invite.

Thanks —
Laura

Subject: Re: Dev-to-prod bridge: SLA, timeouts, and rate-limit playbook

Hey Samir — answering inline: 

1) Batch sizing: with typical M40/A10-like GPU kernels we validate up to 8 examples at ~512 tokens without OOM on our standard 16GB nodes. For your median (420 tokens) we recommend batch_size = 6 for stable throughput; set client-side adaptive batching to cap at 8. If you expect consistent 2k token bursts, use a separate large-context node pool (we can reserve).

2) Node retry pattern (pseudo):

const backoff = (attempt) => Math.min(10000, 200 * Math.pow(2, attempt)) // ms
const jitter = (ms) => Math.random() * ms
async function requestWithRetries(req) {
  for (let i=0;i<4;i++) {
    try {
      return await SDK.call(req)
    } catch (err) {
      if (!shouldRetry(err) || i === 3) throw err
      const wait = backoff(i) + jitter(100)
      await sleep(wait)
    }
  }
}

where shouldRetry(err) returns true for 429 and 5xx only. We also recommend tagging requests with X-RW-Idempotency for safety on POST-like endpoints.

3) Canary plan: yes — start with read-only traffic for 24h (2% traffic), then enable write paths for 12h at 1% before ramping to 10%. We'll provide dashboards (latency, error-rate, token delta) and automatic rollback on 5xx > 1% for 5m.

Operational tips:
- Use our SDK telemetry hooks to forward sample responses (1% sampling) to your observability so you can sanity-check token expansion and hallucination rates.
- Keep a short-lived staging key for canaries; revoke it after cutover.

I'll book a 30m kickoff for Monday 29 Nov at 10am PT (tentative). Laura, do you want me to include implementation runbook as a shared Drive doc?

—Vanessa
